segments.nethackrc:
OPTIONS=name:Probe,role:Valkyrie,race:human,gender:female,align:neutral
OPTIONS=!autopickup,!legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen,pettype:none
OPTIONS=menucolors
MENUCOLOR="[[=foo=]]"=red
MSGTYPE=hide "[b-a]"
AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION="<a{99999}"
MENUCOLOR="a{1}{2}"=red
MSGTYPE=hide "a**"

comment: posixregex.c regex_compile()/regex_match(), from the second host-parity sample (experiments/host-parity/sample2/, recipe re-bad-rc-04): bad patterns in nethackrc: ["[[=foo=]]","[b-a]","a{99999}","a{1}{2}","a**"]. macOS and glibc regex answer differently here. Recorded on macOS, the judge's host, by .github/workflows/macos-recorder.yml (run 44628090866), because regcomp(), regexec() and regerror() differ between macOS and glibc (docs/testing.md, "The regex difference").
